title: Event Isomorphism Program v0

canonical_node.axiom: Lean formalizes event systems and proves exactly what kind of sameness exists between them.
definitions: EventSystem: structure with State, Event, step, invariant, cost.
EventIso: structure-preserving equivalence between EventSystems preserving step, invariant, and cost.
RichEventSystem: extends EventSystem with Gate, coherent, restored, stage, irreversibleFrom.
Sameness Ladder: levels 0-9 classifying strength of event correspondence.
derivation: Loose analogy and bare type equivalence are weak.
Stronger target: preserve transition, invariant, gate, cost, irreversibility, restoration under explicit mapping.
Define minimal EventSystem and EventIso in Lean.
Define richer RichEventSystem and RichEventIso as target architecture.
Classify every event claim using review matrix.
Use negative proofs to show non-arbitrariness within model.
Adopt careful public language to avoid overclaiming.
canonical_node.action: Build Lean 4 no-sorry packages for EventSystem, EventIso, and lemmas; prove first theorem targets; migrate existing claims into stronger framework.
boundary: Does not prove theology from nothing.
Does not claim Lean proves gravity is grace or similar.
Level 9 theological identification is bridge unless explicit theological premises added.
Negative proofs only show failure under encoded constraints, not real-world theological falsehood.
test: Check that EventIso preserves invariant both directions.
Check that EventIso preserves zero-cost and positive-cost events.
Check that EventIso preserves one-step reachability.
Check symmetry and transitivity of EventIso.
Check invalid mapping theorem for toy swap failing cost preservation.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a rigorous framework for proving structure-preserving correspondences between event systems, with explicit preservation of invariants, costs, gates, and irreversibility.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the minimal kernel and existing isomorphism test claims by migrating them into the stronger framework.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this program, event correspondences remain at level of loose analogy or bare type equivalence, lacking rigorous structure preservation.

classification.recommended_atom_action: adopt as research direction; implement Lean packages

overstatement_risks: Claiming Lean proves theological identities without explicit premises.
Overstating negative proofs as disproving real-world interpretations.
Equating formal isomorphism with theological sameness.
kill_conditions: If Lean code cannot be compiled without sorry.
If structure preservation proofs fail for intended mappings.
If public claims exceed what Lean actually verifies.

plain_summary: This document outlines a research program to use Lean 4 to formally prove structure-preserving isomorphisms between event systems from different domains, avoiding overclaiming theological proof. It defines minimal and rich event system structures, a sameness ladder, and a review matrix, with immediate next steps to build Lean packages and prove basic theorems.
